qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Category leadership and Lindy brand recognition across core staples (Clorox bleach, Pine-Sol, Glad, Kingsford, Hidden Valley). Multi-cycle median ROIC of 18.2% and gross margin recovery back to ~44.5% demonstrate brand pricing power, but commoditized chemical formulations face persistent private-label substitution pressure (Great Value, Kirkland).
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 10, REJECT). Mature, heavily US-centric household staples portfolio with flat-to-negative multi-year organic volume growth and severe private-label substitutability across core categories (bleach, trash bags, cat litter). Under Macrotrend 5 (Structural Inflation & Cost of Capital), persistent commodity input cost volatility (resin, chlor-alkali) and elevated refinancing costs on ~$4.0B of debt collide with private-label price ceilings, capping the competitive advantage period below the 15-year hurdle.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC ~18.2%. Revenue has compounded at <2% CAGR over FY15-FY25, with organic volume frequently flat to negative. Gross margin collapsed from 45% to ~36% during the 2021-2023 inflationary shock, requiring aggressive pricing actions to recover to 44.5%, which triggered volume elasticity and trade-downs to store brands. Over 80% of sales remain concentrated in the saturated domestic US market, leaving limited runway for value-accretive capital deployment. Failed M&A diversification in vitamins/supplements (RenewLife/VMS) resulted in major goodwill write-downs and subsequent divestment.
